q: 401. A retaining wall may be built in ...........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist lateral earth pressure and can be constructed using various materials like dry stone (gravity), masonry, or reinforced/plain concrete depending on height and site conditions.

q: 402. A retaining wall is commonly required in the construction of ..........
explain: Retaining walls are essential whenever there is a need to maintain a difference in ground surface elevation, common in hill roads, dam abutments, and bridge wing walls.

q: 403. A stone wall provided to protect the slopes of cutting in natural ground from the action of weather is known as ..........
explain: A breast wall is specifically designed to keep the natural ground slope in situ and protect it from weathering, unlike a retaining wall which usually supports backfill.

q: 404. The total horizontal pressure (p) per meter length of retaining wall at a depth h meter is ..........
explain: According to Rankine's theory, the total active earth pressure is P = 1/2 * w * h² * Ka, where Ka = (1-sinΦ)/(1+sinΦ).

q: 405. A partition wall may be ..........
explain: Partition walls are non-load bearing internal walls used to divide space; they can be permanent (fixed) or movable (folding/collapsible).

q: 406. Plain brick type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Plain brick partitions are typically half-brick thick (10 cm), achieved by laying bricks in the stretcher course.

q: 407. Brick noggin type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Brick nogging consists of a wooden framework (studs and noggins) filled with brickwork, used for stability and speed of construction.

q: 408. In a brick nogging type of partition wall, the vertical wooden members are called ..........
explain: In timber framing or brick nogging, the vertical members are called 'studs' while the horizontal members are 'noggings'.

q: 409. The sill in a wooden partition wall is the .......... wooden member.
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal member of a frame that rests on the floor.

q: 410. The noggin pieces are housed in the studs at a vertical distance of about ..........
explain: For structural stability in a brick nogging wall, horizontal noggins are spaced at intervals of 60 to 90 cm.

q: 411. In constructing concrete partition wall, the concrete mixture usually adopted is ..........
explain: M150 (approx. 1:2:4) is standard for non-structural or lightly loaded concrete partitions.

q: 412. The brick flooring may be done with bricks ..........
options: set at right angle to the walls
laid on edge arranged in herring-bone fashion
explain: Brick flooring is versatile; it can be laid flat, on edge, or in patterns like herring-bone for better aesthetics and strength.

q: 413. A type of flooring made with special aggregate of, marble chips mixed with white and coloured cement, is called ..........
explain: Terrazzo flooring consists of marble chips embedded in a cement binder, then ground and polished to a smooth finish.

q: 414. The moulding provided under nosing to beautify the elevation of a step of stair, is called ..........
explain: Scotia is a decorative concave moulding often placed under the nosing of a tread for aesthetic appeal.

q: 415. The horizontal upper part of a step on which for is placed in ascending or descending a stairway, is called ..........
explain: The tread is the flat, horizontal surface of a step where one places their foot.

q: 416. A series of steps without any platform, break or landing in their direction, is called ..........
explain: A flight is an uninterrupted series of steps between floors or landings.

q: 417. The brick flooring is used in ..........
explain: Due to its durability and low cost, brick flooring is frequently used in warehouses (godowns) and industrial sheds.

q: 418. The flooring made with small pieces of broken tiles of china glazed or of marble arranged in different pattern, is known as ..........
explain: Mosaic flooring involves using small pieces of tile, glass, or stone to create artistic patterns.

q: 419. In stairs, the flier is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: A flier is an ordinary rectangular step in a flight that has a uniform width.

q: 420. In stairs, the soffit is ..........
options: a vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread
a straight step having a parallel width of tread
the under surface of a stair
the angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal
explain: The soffit refers to the underside of a flight of stairs or an arch.

q: 421. The projecting part of the tread beyond the face of riser is called ..........
explain: Nosing is the edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space.

q: 422. In a public building, the stairs should be located near the .......... of building.
explain: In public buildings, stairs should be near the entrance for easy accessibility and fire safety evacuation.

q: 423. The angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal, is called ..........
explain: The pitch is the angle of inclination of the stairs, ideally between 25 and 40 degrees.

q: 424. In stairs, the vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread, is known as ..........
explain: The riser is the vertical member between two treads.

q: 425. The size of a step commonly adopted for residential buildings is ..........
explain: A tread of 270mm and a riser of 150mm is a standard comfortable ratio for residential use.

q: 426. In residential building, the average value of stair width is ..........
explain: A minimum width of 900mm (0.9m) is standard for residential stairs to allow for a single person to move comfortably.

q: 427. The pitch of stair should never exceed ..........
explain: Stairs steeper than 40 degrees are difficult to climb and become dangerous; they are typically kept between 25° and 40°.

q: 428. In designing a stair, the sum of going (in cm) and twice the rise (in cm) should be equal to ..........
explain: The standard comfort formula is (2 * Riser) + Tread = 60 cm (approx).

q: 429. In designing a stair, the product of going (in cm) and twice the rise (in cm) should be equal ..........
explain: Another empirical rule for comfortable stairs is that Tread * Riser should be approximately 400 to 450 cm².

q: 430. The inner surface of an arch is called ..........
explain: The intrados is the lower or inner curve of an arch.

q: 431. The surface of the abutment on which the arch rests, is known as ..........
explain: The skewback is the inclined or splayed surface of an abutment prepared to receive the arch.

q: 432. The highest point on the extrados is called ..........
explain: The crown is the highest part of an arch, where the keystone is located.

q: 433. The vertical distance between the springing line and the highest point on the intrados is called .......... of the arch.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the level of the springing points to the highest point of the intrados.

q: 434. The wedge shaped unit (voussoir) placed at the crown of an arch, is called ..........
explain: The keystone is the central wedge-shaped stone at the summit of an arch, locking the whole together.

q: 435. The perpendicular distance between the intrados and extrados of an arch, is called ..........
explain: Depth or thickness of an arch is the distance between its inner (intrados) and outer (extrados) curves.

q: 436. The arch consisting of fully dressed stones, is called ..........
explain: Ashlar arches use finely dressed stones with thin joints for high-quality architectural work.

q: 437. In a flat arch, the skew back is made to rest in an inclined position so as to make an angle of .......... with the springing line.
explain: In flat arches, the skewback usually makes a 60-degree angle to provide sufficient lateral thrust for stability.

q: 438. The lower portion of an arch between the skew back and crown is called ..........
explain: The haunch is the lower half of the arch, between the crown and the skewback.

q: 439. The vertical members which support the door frame are called ..........
explain: The vertical sides of a frame are referred to as posts (or jambs in some contexts), while styles are the vertical members of the door leaf itself.

q: 440. The external jamb of a door or window opening at right angles to the wall face, is called ..........
explain: Reveals are the vertical sides of an opening that are exposed between the frame and the wall face.

q: 441. A horizontal member of a frame employed to sub-divide a window opening horizontally is called ..........
explain: A transom is a horizontal bar of wood or stone across a window or door.

q: 442. The width of jambs is ..........
explain: Standard jamb width for typical door frames ranges from 7.5cm to 11.5cm.

q: 443. The depth of jambs is ..........
explain: The depth of the jamb or frame section is usually between 60mm and 75mm.

q: 444. The projections which help in securing the head of a door frame to the masonry, are called ..........
explain: Horns are the horizontal projections of the head and sill beyond the vertical posts to fix the frame into the wall.

q: 445. The window used with the object of providing light and air to the end closed space below the roof is called ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof.

q: 446. The window usually provided near the main roof of a room and opens above the adjoining verandah, is called ..........
explain: Clerestory windows are located near the top of a wall, often above an adjacent roof level, to provide light and ventilation to the inner part of a room.

q: 447. For ordinary Portland cement, the initial setting time should not be more than ..........
explain: Standard OPC must have an initial setting time of at least 30 minutes (not 'more than' is likely a typo in the book, as it shouldn't be *less* than 30 mins, but the answer key marks 'a').

q: 448. The cement which is commonly used in all types of structures and require no special consideration is called ..........
explain: Normal setting cement (OPC) is the general-purpose cement used for most construction tasks.

q: 449. The additional of surfactants in the concrete mix results in ..........
options: decrease in the water cement ratio
increase in the strength of concrete
increase in the density of concrete
explain: Surfactants (admixtures) like plasticizers reduce water requirements, which leads to higher density and strength.

q: 450. A fine aggregate is one whose particles are of size ..........
explain: Fine aggregate is defined as material that passes through a 4.75mm IS sieve.

q: 451. A coarse aggregate is one whose particles are of size ..........
explain: Aggregates that are retained on a 4.75 mm IS sieve are classified as coarse aggregates, typically consisting of gravel or crushed stone.

q: 452. The slump commonly adopted for concrete for road works is ..........
explain: Concrete used in road construction needs to be stiff to withstand the vibration of paving machines; a low slump of 25-50 mm is standard.

q: 453. The slump commonly adopted for concrete for columns is ..........
explain: Columns often have dense reinforcement, requiring higher workability (slump of 50-100 mm) to ensure the concrete flows into all spaces without honeycombing.

q: 454. The vertical distance between the wall plate and top of the ridge is called .......... of roof.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the horizontal plane of the eaves (wall plate) to the highest point of the ridge.

q: 455. A rigid formed by the intersection of two sloped surfaces having an exterior angle greater than 180°, is called ..........
explain: A hip is the external angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof surfaces. An internal angle would be called a valley.

q: 456. A block of stone or concrete provided under the end of tie beam to spread the load from the roof over a large of bearing, is called ..........
explain: A template (or bed block) is placed under beams or trusses to distribute concentrated loads over a larger area of the supporting masonry.

q: 457. The horizontal members of wood or steel used to support the common rafter of a sloping roof, are called ..........
explain: Purlins are horizontal structural members that span between trusses or walls to support the common rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 458. In a sloping roof, the inclined wooden members laid from the ridge to the eaves known as ..........
explain: Common rafters extend from the ridge to the eaves and provide the main support for the roof covering.

q: 459. In pitched roofs, the term gable is defined as the ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: A gable is the triangular portion of a wall between the edges of intersecting roof pitches.

q: 460. The term pitch in connection with pitched roofs is defined as a ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: Pitch is the numerical measure of the steepness of a roof, expressed as the ratio of rise to span or as an angle.

q: 461. A pitched roof in which rafters slope to one side only is called ..........
explain: A lean-to roof (also known as a pent or shed roof) consists of a single sloping surface, usually attached to a taller wall.

q: 462. The combination of a king-post truss and queen post truss is known as ..........
explain: A Mansard truss is a 'broken' roof truss that is steeper at the bottom and flatter at the top, effectively combining structural elements to maximize attic space.

q: 463. The coupled roof is suitable for spans upto ..........
explain: Coupled roofs are simple sloping roofs without a tie beam, making them unsuitable for spans exceeding 3.5 meters due to outward thrust.

q: 464. The type of truss commonly used for spans varying from 5 to 9 meter is ..........
explain: A King Post truss utilizes a single central vertical post and is most economical for spans in the range of 5 to 9 meters.

q: 465. In a queen post truss, ....... vertical posts are used.
explain: A Queen Post truss is distinguished by having two vertical tension members (posts) instead of one.

q: 466. A queen post truss is commonly used for spans ..........
explain: Because it has two vertical supports, the Queen Post truss is suitable for larger spans, typically 8 to 12 meters.

q: 467. A couple-close roof is used for spans up to ..........
explain: Adding a horizontal tie beam to a couple roof creates a 'couple-close' roof, extending the safe span to about 5 meters.

q: 468. The pointing which is extensively used in brick work and stone masonry face work, is ..........
explain: Struck pointing (where the upper edge is pressed in) is very common as it sheds water effectively and looks neat.

q: 469. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joints and then finished off flush with the edges of the bricks or stones, is called ..........
explain: Flush pointing is the simplest form, where the mortar is finished level with the face of the masonry.

q: 470. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joints and then finished off flush with the face of the bricks or stones, is called ..........
explain: In tuck pointing, a groove is made in the flush mortar and filled with a narrow strip of white putty to give the illusion of very fine joints.

q: 471. The process of filling up all nail holes, cracks etc. with putty is known as ..........
explain: Stopping involves using putty or wood filler to smooth out surface imperfections before painting.

q: 472. Pile foundation are provided ..........
explain: Piles are deep foundations used when surface soil is weak, water-logged, or compressible, to transfer loads to deeper, firmer strata.

q: 473. In pile foundation when the load is supported by friction between the pile and surrounding soil and also by resting the pile on hard stratum, such a pile is known as ..........
explain: Most piles rely on a combination of skin friction along the sides and end-bearing at the tip.

q: 474. A type of foundation in which a cantilever beam is used for joining the two footings is ..........
explain: A strap footing connects two individual footings with a rigid beam (strap), often used when one footing is on a property line.

q: 475. For supporting a heavy structure in a sandy soil, the type of foundation generally preferred is ..........
explain: A raft (mat) foundation covers the entire area under the building, which helps reduce differential settlement in sandy or weak soils.

q: 476. The depth of excavation for foundation is usually checked with a ..........
explain: Boning rods are T-shaped wooden rods used in sets to maintain or check the correct levels and depths of trenches.

q: 477. Generally for a column in a workshop using Gantry cranes, the foundation to be used should be..........
explain: Grillage foundation is used to transmit heavy loads from steel columns to a soil of low bearing capacity without requiring great depth.

q: 478. For an ordinary double storey building, the type of foundation to be used should be ..........
explain: Spread footings are the most common and economical choice for standard low-rise residential buildings on stable soil.

q: 479. For a bridge pier, in very deep water the foundation to be used should be ..........
explain: Caissons are hollow structures sunk into the ground or water, then filled with concrete, making them ideal for bridge piers in deep water.

q: 480. The type of masonry in which the stones of the same height are used and the courses are also of the same height is called ..........
explain: In coursed rubble masonry, stones are roughly squared and laid in distinct horizontal layers (courses).

q: 481. The type of masonry in which the stones of irregular size and shapes are used and there are no regular course is called ..........
explain: Random rubble masonry is the most basic and cheapest form of stone walling, using stones as they come from the quarry.

q: 482. The type of masonry in which the stones are fine chisel dressed and the thickness of joints does not exceed 3 mm is called ..........
explain: Ashlar fine masonry uses perfectly squared, dressed stones with very thin mortar joints for a superior finish.

q: 483. Pile are usually not made of ..........
explain: Stainless steel is too expensive for structural foundation piles; standard steel, timber, and reinforced concrete are used instead.

q: 484. When two blocks of stone have a tendency to be pulled apart in the direction of their lengths, then the type of joint used is called ..........
explain: A cramped joint uses a small metal 'cramp' (like a staple) to tie two stones together and resist tension.

q: 485. If after every three or four stretchers, one header is used in a brick masonry wall, then the bond so formed will be called as ..........
explain: English Garden Wall bond consists of several courses of stretchers followed by a single course of headers.

q: 486. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as ..........
explain: Breast walls protect natural earth slopes from erosion and weathering, whereas retaining walls support man-made fills.

q: 487. The stretcher bond is generally used for ..........
explain: Stretcher bond is only suitable for walls that are half-brick thick (10 cm), like partition walls.

q: 488. Herringbone bond is used for ..........
options: architectural finish to the face work
walls having thickness more than 4 bricks
explain: Herringbone bond is a decorative pattern where bricks are laid at 45 degrees, common in flooring and very thick walls.

q: 489. To construct a 10 cm thick partition wall, preferred bond will be ..........
explain: A 10 cm wall is exactly the width of a single brick's length (stretcher side), hence stretcher bond is used.

q: 490. An external corner in brick masonry is called ..........
explain: The term quoin refers to the external corner of a wall or the stones/bricks used to form it.

q: 491. The part of a wall at the side of an opening in the masonry is called ..........
explain: Jambs are the vertical sides of an opening for a door or window.

q: 492. The nominal thickness of an expansion joints in brick wall must be more than ..........
explain: Expansion joints allow for thermal movement and are typically at least 20 mm wide.

q: 493. The operation finishing mortar joints after completion of a masonry wall is called ..........
explain: Pointing is the process of raking out mortar joints to a depth of 13-20 mm and refilling them with superior mortar.

q: 494. The brick arranged systematically and bedded together in mortar to form a homogeneous mass capable of withstanding and transmitting forces is known as ..........
explain: This is the general definition of brick masonry as a structural system.

q: 495. Dry bricks are recommended in brick masonry when the mortar used is ..........
explain: Bricks should be soaked for cement/lime mortar, but with mud mortar, dry bricks are often used to prevent the mud from becoming too runny.

q: 496. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall ..........
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting and spreading mortar and for cutting bricks.

q: 497. Frogs made in the bricks are ..........
options: to reduce weight of the brick
to form a key for holding the mortar
to indicate year and name of the manufacture
to indicate top of the brick
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top face of the brick that creates a mechanical bond (key) with the mortar.

q: 498. In any case the bearing of a lintel should not be less than ..........
explain: Standard practice dictates a minimum bearing (overlap on the wall) of 15 cm or 1/10th to 1/12th of the span.

q: 499. In R.C.C. lintels the positions of main reinforcement in concrete should be at ..........
explain: Lintels act like beams; they experience tension at the bottom, so reinforcement must be placed in the bottom zone.

q: 500. For large spans the most suitable type of roof preferred is ..........
explain: Shell roofs are thin, curved R.C.C. structures that can cover very large spans without intermediate columns.
